subject: Packaging & pricing: long-term retention, tracing and dashboards
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Eric Lowe <eric@finx.io>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-ons: retention + tracing + dashboards — high level ask

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're putting together an internal ask for long-term observability at Acme Analytics and I wanted to surface the key requirements so your team can propose packaging and pricing that aligns with our procurement window (targeting a Dec contract).

Top-level needs:
- Logs + spans retention: cold archive for long-term compliance, ~2 years for logs, 90 days for traces.
- Advanced dashboards: live traces + drilldowns for SRE and product analytics teams (approx 10 power users).
- Ingest profile: steady 30 TB/month, periodic spikes during product launches.

Questions for Redwood:
1) How do you structure a SKU for archive vs hot retention? Do you have blended discounts for combined retention + tracing + dashboard bundles?
2) What crediting or pilot credits can you offer for a POC?
3) Are there fixed fees (seats/licenses) for advanced dashboards in addition to ingest/retention?

If you could send a short options matrix (pilot -> mid -> committed) and a sample SOW format, that would help us accelerate procurement. I've looped in Eric from our platform team for technical clarifications.

Cheers,

Sasha Patel
Head of Platform
Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme-observability-requirements-10-26.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Eric Lowe <eric@finx.io>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons: retention + tracing + dashboards — high level ask

Hi Sasha,

Thanks — this is great detail and exactly what we need to scope a few packaged options. I'll put together a short matrix and SOW sketch. Quick answers inline:

- SKU structure: We separate hot (30-90d) and cold (6-24mo) retention. Hot retention is metered on ingest/ingress with per-GB active storage; cold archival is a lower $/GB/month rate with retrieval fees. Bundles reduce the per-GB archival rate by up to 35% depending on commit.
- Bundles & discounts: Yes — combined bundles (tracing + dashboards + retention) receive an additional additive discount that grows with committed annual spend. We can model pilot credits for POCs.
- Dashboards: There is a seat-based component (power users) plus a per-query execution cost for heavy live trace joins. For your 10 power users we usually propose an annual seat fee plus an ingestion/retention allowance.

I'll share a draft matrix and a sample SOW by EOD. Attaching a pricing workbook with placeholders for your numbers — please replace the ingest spikes to let us re-calc.

Best,

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention-pricing-workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme observability pricing request — discount recommendation

Kimberly / Jordan,

Forwarding Sasha's ask. Acme is looking at a Dec procurement; they want a matrix that shows pilot -> mid -> committed. They are steady 30 TB/month with spikes, 2y cold retention, 90d traces, 10 power users.

My draft thoughts:
- Pilot: 3-month POC with $15k in usage credits (covering ~10 TB ingest + 90d retention), standard metered rates otherwise; no seat fees.
- Mid (12mo): 20% off list for combined bundle, 12mo commit, 1.25x overage cushion. No archival discount.
- Committed (24mo): 32% off list on combined bundle, archival rate reduced by 30%, waived retrieval fees for first 5TB/month. Seat fees discounted 40% first year.

Question: Do we have flexibility to offer an incremental concession on the committed tier (extra 3-5% off) if they commit to a two-year 300k minimum? Also want to include a clause for usage re-evaluation at 12 months.

Jordan — can you run quick margin impact on the 32% committed scenario with archival cutouts? Kimberly — any guardrails from legal on the 2y minimum + retrieval waiver?

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme observability pricing request — discount recommendation

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 09:07 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kimberly / Jordan,
>
> Forwarding Sasha's ask. Acme is looking at a Dec procurement; they want a matrix that shows pilot -> mid -> committed. They are steady 30 TB/month with spikes, 2y cold retention, 90d traces, 10 power users.
>
> My draft thoughts:
> - Pilot: 3-month POC with $15k in usage credits (covering ~10 TB ingest + 90d retention), standard metered rates otherwise; no seat fees.
> - Mid (12mo): 20% off list for combined bundle, 12mo commit, 1.25x overage cushion. No archival discount.
> - Committed (24mo): 32% off list on combined bundle, archival rate reduced by 30%, waived retrieval fees for first 5TB/month. Seat fees discounted 40% first year.
>
> Question: Do we have flexibility to offer an incremental concession on the committed tier (extra 3-5% off) if they commit to a two-year 300k minimum? Also want to include a clause for usage re-evaluation at 12 months.

Marcus / Kimberly — quick notes after a fast pass on margin modeling:
- Committed 32% across-the-board is aggressive but doable if we constrain waived retrievals and make excess retrievals billable post 5TB. If they guarantee $300k ARR minimum over 2 years, we can do an incremental 4% off list (so effectively 36% off list) but that requires a signed SOW and payment terms: net30 + 50% upfront.
- Recommend we add a CPI-linked price review at month 12 (or usage reforecast clause) to protect economics.
- Seat fee concessions fine, but cap seat count reductions to avoid indefinite unlimited users.

Kimberly — legal/finance signoffs needed on the upfront 50% and on the retrieval waiver language. If they push for net60 we should tighten the upfront commitment.

I'll draft a short commercial term snippet to include with the matrix.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Director, Commercial

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acme.com>, Eric Lowe <eric@finx.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Acme options: pilot, standard annual, committed 24mo — pricing snapshot and next steps

Sasha / Eric,

Appreciate the details — we pulled together three options for Acme (attached workbook + SOW sketch). High level:

1) Pilot (3 months)
- $15k usage credit to cover initial ingest and 90d retention for the trial cluster.
- No seat fees during pilot.
- Standard metered rates apply for overage.

2) Standard annual (12 months)
- 20% off list for combined bundle (tracing + dashboards + retention).
- 1.25x overage cushion for the first 6 months.
- Archival billed at list archival rate.

3) Committed (24 months) — preferred economics
- 32% off list on the combined bundle.
- Archival rate reduced by 30% and retrieval waived for first 5TB/month.
- Seat fees: 40% discount first year for up to 12 seats, then revert to standard.
- If Acme commits to a $300k minimum over 24 months and 50% upfront payment on signature, we can extend an incremental 4% additional discount (effective 36% off list).

Commercial guardrails we propose:
- 12-month usage reforecast (price review) to re-align economics if ingest deviates >30% from baseline.
- Retrieval waiver limited to 5TB/month and subject to fair-use clause.
- Overages revert to list rates post cushion.

Next steps: review the attached workbook (retention-pricing-workbook.xlsx) with your ingest spike assumptions and we can run a granular model. If this looks directionally right, propose a 30-minute call next week to walk the SOW draft and get procurement alignment.

Thanks — happy to adjust.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-observability-sow-v2.pdf (application/pdf); retention-pricing-workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)
